01 / The missing layer

Your agent can click.
Can your business depend on it?

The workflow works in the demo. Then the website changes.

Valuable operations live behind supplier portals, internal tools, and websites without usable APIs. A one-off script can reach them. A business dependency needs a contract, evidence, safe recovery, and someone to maintain it.

Wrong recordA successful click can still be the wrong action.
Unknown outcomeA timeout after a write makes a blind retry dangerous.
Quiet driftThe page still loads. The integration no longer means the same thing.
02 / Our bet

As the interface moves to AI,
the API becomes the product.

We believe people will bring capabilities into the clients where they already work, instead of opening another dashboard for every task.

The familiar modelBuild an app.
Bring users to it.
The Pixie visionBuild a capability.
Bring it to the user.

04 / Agents build. Scripts run. Agents repair.
Intelligence when needed.
Predictability by default.
01 — AUTHOR
Show the workflow.
Ultrafast explores the browser. Pixie captures the steps and helps generate parameterized code with explicit acceptance checks.
02 — EXECUTE
Run the tested script.
Normal execution uses no model calls. Every run still checks identity, completeness, and permitted side effects.
03 — MAINTAIN
Repair the implementation.
When a site changes, propose a patch. Test it against the existing contract. Review before promotion.
Maintenance loop / illustrative scenarioContract v1 stays fixed
Script verified→Change detected→Patch tested→Human approval
The script reads invoices and passes its checks. No model is called.
A locator repair is different from a business-rule change. An uncertain write stops for reconciliation; it is never blindly replayed.

06 / Evidence before ambition
We have a prototype.
Now we test the harder promise.
OBSERVED IN THE PROTOTYPE
Verified browser-backed CRUD.
  • Local Todo create, read, rename, and delete passed live checks.
  • Duplicate targets, missing targets, and disallowed titles required review.
  • Request replay reused the original run; conflicting payloads were rejected.
  • Hacker News exposed a gap: schema-valid data can still fail the intended meaning.
NEXT EXPERIMENT · NOT YET BUILT
Preserve the contract through change.
  • Generate scripts from agent-assisted authoring.
  • Prove normal execution makes zero model calls.
  • Change a controlled website and propose a repair.
  • Pass unchanged checks, approve promotion, and demonstrate rollback.
  • Recover from a timeout after a write without duplicating it.
Prototype evidence is from local testing, not production customer traction. Autonomous repair, generated interfaces, and client integrations are proposed capabilities.


07 / A focused entry point. A framework-sized ambition.
Start with one workflow.
Grow into the API layer.
FIRST
Prove the repair loop.
A controlled Todo experiment. Generated scripts, frozen tests, safe recovery, and reviewed repairs.
THEN
Serve repeatable portal work.
Target developers connecting business systems without suitable APIs. Add contracts, asynchronous runs, and a usable developer workflow.
EVENTUALLY
Describe any capability.
Combine browser workflows, APIs, and data sources. Publish through REST, GraphQL, and MCP. Maintain them together.
